audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 13, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness and reception-history audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for altar prophecy, future corpse desecration, temporary hand impairment, healing, prophetic boundaries, deceptive revelation claims, spiritual manipulation, lion death, animal-sign interpretation, mourning, burial, class language, and religious-political critique.

verses.restored: Look, a man of Divine came from Judah by word of YHWH to Bethel, while Jeroboam stood by altar to burn incense.

familiar.text: And, behold, there came a man of God out of Judah by the word of the LORD unto Bethel: and Jeroboam stood by the altar to burn incense.

modern.text: Suddenly, as Jeroboam was standing beside the altar to burn incense, there came a man of God from Judah to Bethel by the word of the LORD.

original.text: וְהִנֵּ֣ה אִ֣ישׁ אֱלֹהִ֗ים בָּ֧א מִיהוּדָ֛ה בִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל בֵּֽית אֵ֑ל וְיָרָבְעָ֛ם עֹמֵ֥ד עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לְהַקְטִֽיר

verses.restored: He cried against altar by word of YHWH: Altar, altar, thus says YHWH: Look, a son shall be born to house of David, Josiah by name. Upon you he shall sacrifice priests of high places who burn incense upon you, and human bones shall be burned upon you.

familiar.text: And he cried against the altar in the word of the LORD, and said, O altar, altar, thus saith the LORD; Behold, a child shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name; and upon thee shall he offer the priests of the high places that burn incense upon thee, and men’s bones shall be burnt upon thee.

modern.text: And he cried out against the altar by the word of the LORD, “O altar, O altar, this is what the LORD says: ‘A son named Josiah will be born to the house of David, and upon you he will sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense upon you, and human bones will be burned upon you.’”

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֤א עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ בִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ מִזְבֵּ֣חַ מִזְבֵּ֔חַ כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה הִנֵּֽה בֵ֞ן נוֹלָ֤ד לְבֵית דָּוִד֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ שְׁמ֔וֹ וְזָבַ֣ח עָלֶ֗יךָ אֶת כֹּהֲנֵ֤י הַבָּמוֹת֙ הַמַּקְטִרִ֣ים עָלֶ֔יךָ וְעַצְמ֥וֹת אָדָ֖ם יִשְׂרְפ֥וּ עָלֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: He gave a sign that day: This is sign YHWH spoke—look, altar shall split and ashes upon it shall be poured out.

familiar.text: And he gave a sign the same day, saying, This is the sign which the LORD hath spoken; Behold, the altar shall be rent, and the ashes that are upon it shall be poured out.

modern.text: That day the man of God gave a sign, saying, “The LORD has spoken this sign: ‘Surely the altar will be split apart, and the ashes upon it will be poured out.’”

original.text: וְנָתַן֩ בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֤וּא מוֹפֵת֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר זֶ֣ה הַמּוֹפֵ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה הִנֵּ֤ה הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ נִקְרָ֔ע וְנִשְׁפַּ֖ךְ הַדֶּ֥שֶׁן אֲשֶׁר עָלָֽיו

verses.restored: When king heard word man of Divine cried against altar in Bethel, Jeroboam stretched his hand from altar, saying, Seize him. His hand which he stretched against him withered/was immobilized, and he could not draw it back to himself.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when king Jeroboam heard the saying of the man of God, which had cried against the altar in Bethel, that he put forth his hand from the altar, saying, Lay hold on him. And his hand, which he put forth against him, dried up, so that he could not pull it in again to him.

modern.text: Now when King Jeroboam, who was at the altar in Bethel, heard the word that the man of God had cried out against it, he stretched out his hand and said, “Seize him!” But the hand he stretched out toward him withered, so that he could not pull it back.

original.text: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת דְּבַ֣ר אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר קָרָ֤א עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ בְּבֵֽית אֵ֔ל וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יָרָבְעָ֧ם אֶת יָד֛וֹ מֵעַ֥ל הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לֵאמֹ֣ר תִּפְשֻׂ֑הוּ וַתִּיבַ֤שׁ יָדוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁלַ֣ח עָלָ֔יו וְלֹ֥א יָכֹ֖ל לַהֲשִׁיבָ֥הּ אֵלָֽיו

verses.restored: The altar split and ashes poured from altar according to sign man of Divine gave by word of YHWH.

familiar.text: The altar also was rent, and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of God had given by the word of the LORD.

modern.text: And the altar was split apart, and the ashes poured out, according to the sign that the man of God had given by the word of the LORD.

original.text: וְהַמִּזְבֵּ֣חַ נִקְרָ֔ע וַיִּשָּׁפֵ֥ךְ הַדֶּ֖שֶׁן מִן הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ כַּמּוֹפֵ֗ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֛ן אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: The king answered man of Divine, Please entreat face of YHWH your Divine and pray for me, that my hand may be restored. Man of Divine entreated face of YHWH, and king's hand was restored and became as before.

familiar.text: And the king answered and said unto the man of God, Intreat now the face of the LORD thy God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored me again. And the man of God besought the LORD, and the king’s hand was restored him again, and became as it was before.

modern.text: Then the king responded to the man of God, “Intercede with the LORD your God and pray that my hand may be restored.” So the man of God interceded with the LORD, and the king’s hand was restored to him as it was before.

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַן הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים חַל נָ֞א אֶת פְּנֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ וְהִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל בַּעֲדִ֔י וְתָשֹׁ֥ב יָדִ֖י אֵלָ֑י וַיְחַ֤ל אִישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַתָּ֤שָׁב יַד הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֵלָ֔יו וַתְּהִ֖י כְּבָרִֽאשֹׁנָֽה

verses.restored: The king said to man of Divine, Come home with me and refresh yourself, and I will give you a gift.

familiar.text: And the king said unto the man of God, Come home with me, and refresh thyself, and I will give thee a reward.

modern.text: Then the king said to the man of God, “Come home with me and refresh yourself, and I will give you a reward.”

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶל אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים בֹּאָה אִתִּ֥י הַבַּ֖יְתָה וּֽסְעָ֑דָה וְאֶתְּנָ֥ה לְךָ֖ מַתָּֽת

verses.restored: Man of Divine said to king, If you give me half your house, I will not go with you, nor eat bread or drink water in this place.

familiar.text: And the man of God said unto the king, If thou wilt give me half thine house, I will not go in with thee, neither will I eat bread nor drink water in this place:

modern.text: But the man of God replied, “If you were to give me half your possessions, I still would not go with you, nor would I eat bread or drink water in this place.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אִישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אִם תִּתֶּן לִי֙ אֶת חֲצִ֣י בֵיתֶ֔ךָ לֹ֥א אָבֹ֖א עִמָּ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא אֹ֤כַל לֶ֨חֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א אֶשְׁתֶּה מַּ֔יִם בַּמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: For thus I was commanded by word of YHWH: You shall not eat bread or drink water or return by way you came.

familiar.text: For so was it charged me by the word of the LORD, saying, Eat no bread, nor drink water, nor turn again by the same way that thou camest.

modern.text: For this is what I was commanded by the word of the LORD: ‘You must not eat bread or drink water or return by the way you came.’”

original.text: כִּֽי כֵ֣ן צִוָּ֣ה אֹתִ֗י בִּדְבַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹא תֹ֥אכַל לֶ֖חֶם וְלֹ֣א תִשְׁתֶּה מָּ֑יִם וְלֹ֣א תָשׁ֔וּב בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלָֽכְתָּ

verses.restored: He went by another way and did not return by way he came to Bethel.

familiar.text: So he went another way, and returned not by the way that he came to Bethel.

modern.text: So the man of God went another way and did not return by the way he had come to Bethel. The Old Prophet and the Man of God

original.text: וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ אַחֵ֑ר וְלֹֽא שָׁ֣ב בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֛ר בָּ֥א בָ֖הּ אֶל בֵּֽית אֵֽל

verses.restored: An old prophet lived in Bethel. His sons came and recounted to him all work man of Divine did that day in Bethel and words he spoke to king.

familiar.text: Now there dwelt an old prophet in Bethel; and his sons came and told him all the works that the man of God had done that day in Bethel: the words which he had spoken unto the king, them they told also to their father.

modern.text: Now a certain old prophet was living in Bethel, and his sons came and told him all the deeds that the man of God had done that day in Bethel. They also told their father the words that the man had spoken to the king.

original.text: וְנָבִ֤יא אֶחָד֙ זָקֵ֔ן יֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּבֵֽית אֵ֑ל וַיָּב֣וֹא בְנ֡וֹ וַיְסַפֶּר ל֣וֹ אֶת כָּל הַמַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה֩ אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֨ים הַיּ֜וֹם בְּבֵֽית אֵ֗ל אֶת הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַֽיְסַפְּר֖וּם לַאֲבִיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Their father said, Which way did he go? His sons had seen way man of Divine from Judah went.

familiar.text: And their father said unto them, What way went he? For his sons had seen what way the man of God went, which came from Judah.

modern.text: “Which way did he go?” their father asked. And his sons showed him the way taken by the man of God, who had come from Judah.

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר אֲלֵהֶם֙ אֲבִיהֶ֔ם אֵֽי זֶ֥ה הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ הָלָ֑ךְ וַיִּרְא֣וּ בָנָ֗יו אֶת הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָלַךְ֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר בָּ֖א מִיהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: He said to his sons, Saddle donkey for me. They saddled donkey, and he rode upon it.

familiar.text: And he said unto his sons, Saddle me the ass. So they saddled him the ass: and he rode thereon,

modern.text: So the prophet said to his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.” Then they saddled the donkey for him, and he mounted it

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל בָּנָ֔יו חִבְשׁוּ לִ֖י הַחֲמ֑וֹר וַיַּחְבְּשׁוּ ל֣וֹ הַחֲמ֔וֹר וַיִּרְכַּ֖ב עָלָֽיו

verses.restored: He went after man of Divine and found him sitting beneath terebinth/oak. He said, Are you man of Divine who came from Judah? He said, I am.

familiar.text: And went after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak: and he said unto him, Art thou the man of God that camest from Judah? And he said, I am.

modern.text: and went after the man of God. He found him sitting under an oak tree and asked, “Are you the man of God who came from Judah?” “I am,” he replied.

original.text: וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיִּ֨מְצָאֵ֔הוּ יֹשֵׁ֖ב תַּ֣חַת הָאֵלָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו הַאַתָּ֧ה אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אתָ מִֽיהוּדָ֖ה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אָֽנִי

verses.restored: He said to him, Come home with me and eat bread.

familiar.text: Then he said unto him, Come home with me, and eat bread.

modern.text: So the prophet said to the man of God, “Come home with me and eat some bread.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו לֵ֥ךְ אִתִּ֖י הַבָּ֑יְתָה וֶאֱכֹ֖ל לָֽחֶם

verses.restored: He said, I cannot return with you or go with you, nor will I eat bread or drink water with you in this place.

familiar.text: And he said, I may not return with thee, nor go in with thee: neither will I eat bread nor drink water with thee in this place:

modern.text: But the man replied, “I cannot return with you or eat bread or drink water with you in this place.

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לֹ֥א אוּכַ֛ל לָשׁ֥וּב אִתָּ֖ךְ וְלָב֣וֹא אִתָּ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא אֹ֣כַל לֶ֗חֶם וְלֹֽא אֶשְׁתֶּ֤ה אִתְּךָ֙ מַ֔יִם בַּמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: For word came to me by word of YHWH: You shall not eat bread or drink water there or return by way you came.

familiar.text: For it was said to me by the word of the LORD, Thou shalt eat no bread nor drink water there, nor turn again to go by the way that thou camest.

modern.text: For I have been told by the word of the LORD: ‘You must not eat bread or drink water there or return by the way you came.’”

original.text: כִּֽי דָבָ֤ר אֵלַי֙ בִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה לֹֽא תֹאכַ֣ל לֶ֔חֶם וְלֹֽא תִשְׁתֶּ֥ה שָׁ֖ם מָ֑יִם לֹא תָשׁ֣וּב לָלֶ֔כֶת בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר הָלַ֥כְתָּ בָּֽהּ

verses.restored: He said to him, I also am a prophet like you, and a messenger spoke to me by word of YHWH, saying, Bring him back with you to your house so he may eat bread and drink water. But he lied to him.

familiar.text: He said unto him, I am a prophet also as thou art; and an angel spake unto me by the word of the LORD, saying, Bring him back with thee into thine house, that he may eat bread and drink water. But he lied unto him.

modern.text: Then the prophet replied, “I too am a prophet like you, and an angel spoke to me by the word of the LORD, saying, ‘Bring him back with you to your house, so that he may eat bread and drink water.’” The old prophet was lying to him,

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ גַּם אֲנִ֣י נָבִיא֮ כָּמוֹךָ֒ וּמַלְאָ֡ךְ דִּבֶּ֣ר אֵלַי֩ בִּדְבַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר הֲשִׁבֵ֤הוּ אִתְּךָ֙ אֶל בֵּיתֶ֔ךָ וְיֹ֥אכַל לֶ֖חֶם וְיֵ֣שְׁתְּ מָ֑יִם כִּחֵ֖שׁ לֽוֹ

verses.restored: So he returned with him, ate bread in his house, and drank water.

familiar.text: So he went back with him, and did eat bread in his house, and drank water.

modern.text: but the man of God went back with him, ate bread in his house, and drank water.

original.text: וַיָּ֣שָׁב אִתּ֗וֹ וַיֹּ֥אכַל לֶ֛חֶם בְּבֵית֖וֹ וַיֵּ֥שְׁתְּ מָֽיִם

verses.restored: As they sat at table, word of YHWH came to prophet who brought him back.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as they sat at the table, that the word of the LORD came unto the prophet that brought him back:

modern.text: While they were sitting at the table, the word of the LORD came to the prophet who had brought him back,

original.text: וַיְהִ֕י הֵ֥ם יֹשְׁבִ֖ים אֶל הַשֻּׁלְחָ֑ן וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל הַנָּבִ֖יא אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֱשִׁיבֽוֹ

verses.restored: He cried to man of Divine who came from Judah: Thus says YHWH: Because you rebelled against mouth of YHWH and did not guard command YHWH your Divine commanded you,

familiar.text: And he cried unto the man of God that came from Judah, saying, Thus saith the LORD, Forasmuch as thou hast disobeyed the mouth of the LORD, and hast not kept the commandment which the LORD thy God commanded thee,

modern.text: and the prophet cried out to the man of God who had come from Judah, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Because you have defied the word of the LORD and have not kept the commandment that the LORD your God gave you,

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֞א אֶל אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר בָּ֤א מִֽיהוּדָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה יַ֗עַן כִּ֤י מָרִ֨יתָ֙ פִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹ֤א שָׁמַ֨רְתָּ֙ אֶת הַמִּצְוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוְּךָ֖ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: but returned and ate bread and drank water in place of which YHWH said, Eat no bread and drink no water, your corpse shall not come to tomb of your ancestors.

familiar.text: But camest back, and hast eaten bread and drunk water in the place, of the which the Lord did say to thee, Eat no bread, and drink no water; thy carcase shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers.

modern.text: but you went back and ate bread and drank water in the place where He told you not to do so, your body shall never reach the tomb of your fathers.’”

original.text: וַתָּ֗שָׁב וַתֹּ֤אכַל לֶ֨חֶם֙ וַתֵּ֣שְׁתְּ מַ֔יִם בַּמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר אֵלֶ֔יךָ אַל תֹּ֥אכַל לֶ֖חֶם וְאַל תֵּ֣שְׁתְּ מָ֑יִם לֹֽא תָב֥וֹא נִבְלָתְךָ֖ אֶל קֶ֥בֶר אֲבֹתֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: After he ate bread and drank, old prophet saddled donkey for prophet he had brought back.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, after he had eaten bread, and after he had drunk, that he saddled for him the ass, to wit, for the prophet whom he had brought back.

modern.text: And after the man of God had finished eating and drinking, the old prophet who had brought him back saddled the donkey for him.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחֲרֵ֛י אָכְל֥וֹ לֶ֖חֶם וְאַחֲרֵ֣י שְׁתוֹת֑וֹ וַיַּחֲבָשׁ ל֣וֹ הַחֲמ֔וֹר לַנָּבִ֖יא אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֱשִׁיבֽוֹ

verses.restored: He went, and a lion met him on road and killed him. His corpse was cast upon road, and donkey stood beside it; lion also stood beside corpse.

familiar.text: And when he was gone, a lion met him by the way, and slew him: and his carcase was cast in the way, and the ass stood by it, the lion also stood by the carcase.

modern.text: As he went on his way, a lion met him on the road and killed him, and his body was left lying in the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it.

original.text: וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ וַיִּמְצָאֵ֧הוּ אַרְיֵ֛ה בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ וַיְמִיתֵ֑הוּ וַתְּהִ֤י נִבְלָתוֹ֙ מֻשְׁלֶ֣כֶת בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְהַחֲמוֹר֙ עֹמֵ֣ד אֶצְלָ֔הּ וְהָ֣אַרְיֵ֔ה עֹמֵ֖ד אֵ֥צֶל הַנְּבֵלָֽה

verses.restored: Look, people passed and saw corpse cast upon road and lion standing beside corpse. They came and spoke in city where old prophet lived.

familiar.text: And, behold, men passed by, and saw the carcase cast in the way, and the lion standing by the carcase: and they came and told it in the city where the old prophet dwelt.

modern.text: And there were men passing by who saw the body lying in the road with the lion standing beside it, and they went and reported this in the city where the old prophet lived.

original.text: וְהִנֵּ֧ה אֲנָשִׁ֣ים עֹבְרִ֗ים וַיִּרְא֤וּ אֶת הַנְּבֵלָה֙ מֻשְׁלֶ֣כֶת בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְאֶת הָ֣אַרְיֵ֔ה עֹמֵ֖ד אֵ֣צֶל הַנְּבֵלָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ וַיְדַבְּר֣וּ בָעִ֔יר אֲשֶׁ֛ר הַנָּבִ֥יא הַזָּקֵ֖ן יֹשֵׁ֥ב בָּֽהּ

verses.restored: Prophet who brought him back heard and said, It is man of Divine who rebelled against mouth of YHWH; therefore YHWH gave him to lion, which broke him and killed him, according to word YHWH spoke to him.

familiar.text: And when the prophet that brought him back from the way heard thereof, he said, It is the man of God, who was disobedient unto the word of the LORD: therefore the LORD hath delivered him unto the lion, which hath torn him, and slain him, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake unto him.

modern.text: When the prophet who had brought him back from his journey heard this, he said, “It is the man of God who disobeyed the command of the LORD. Therefore the LORD has delivered him to the lion, and it has mauled him and killed him, according to the word that the LORD had spoken to him.”

verses.restored: He spoke to his sons, Saddle donkey for me. They saddled it.

familiar.text: And he spake to his sons, saying, Saddle me the ass. And they saddled him.

modern.text: Then the old prophet instructed his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.” So they saddled it,

verses.restored: The prophet lifted corpse of man of Divine, placed it upon donkey, and brought it back. Old prophet came to city to mourn and bury him.

familiar.text: And the prophet took up the carcase of the man of God, and laid it upon the ass, and brought it back: and the old prophet came to the city, to mourn and to bury him.

modern.text: So the old prophet lifted up the body of the man of God, laid it on the donkey, and brought it back to his own city to mourn for him and bury him.

familiar.text: And he laid his carcase in his own grave; and they mourned over him, saying, Alas, my brother!

modern.text: Then he laid the body in his own tomb, and they lamented over him, “Oh, my brother!”

original.text: וַיַּנַּ֥ח אֶת נִבְלָת֖וֹ בְּקִבְר֑וֹ וַיִּסְפְּד֥וּ עָלָ֖יו ה֥וֹי אָחִֽי

verses.restored: For word he cried by word of YHWH against altar in Bethel and against all houses of high places in cities of Samaria shall surely come to pass.

familiar.text: For the saying which he cried by the word of the LORD against the altar in Bethel, and against all the houses of the high places which are in the cities of Samaria, shall surely come to pass.

modern.text: for the message that he cried out by the word of the LORD against the altar in Bethel and against all the shrines on the high places in the cities of Samaria will surely come to pass.”

original.text: כִּי֩ הָיֹ֨ה יִהְיֶ֜ה הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֤ר קָרָא֙ בִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּבֵֽית אֵ֑ל וְעַל֙ כָּל בָּתֵּ֣י הַבָּמ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעָרֵ֥י שֹׁמְרֽוֹן

verses.restored: After this matter Jeroboam did not turn from his evil way, but again made priests of high places from all the people. Whoever desired, he filled his hand, and the person became priest of high places.

familiar.text: After this thing Jeroboam returned not from his evil way, but made again of the lowest of the people priests of the high places: whosoever would, he consecrated him, and he became one of the priests of the high places.

modern.text: Even after these events, Jeroboam did not repent of his evil ways, but again he appointed priests for the high places from every class of people. He ordained anyone who desired to be a priest of the high places.

original.text: אַחַר֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה לֹֽא שָׁ֥ב יָרָבְעָ֖ם מִדַּרְכּ֣וֹ הָרָעָ֑ה וַ֠יָּשָׁב וַיַּ֜עַשׂ מִקְצ֤וֹת הָעָם֙ כֹּהֲנֵ֣י בָמ֔וֹת הֶֽחָפֵץ֙ יְמַלֵּ֣א אֶת יָד֔וֹ וִיהִ֖י כֹּהֲנֵ֥י בָמֽוֹת

verses.restored: This matter became sin to house of Jeroboam, to cut it off and destroy it from face of earth.

familiar.text: And this thing became sin unto the house of Jeroboam, even to cut it off, and to destroy it from off the face of the earth.

modern.text: And this was the sin of the house of Jeroboam that led to its extermination and destruction from the face of the earth.

original.text: וַיְהִי֙ בַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה לְחַטַּ֖את בֵּ֣ית יָרָבְעָ֑ם וּלְהַכְחִיד֙ וּלְהַשְׁמִ֔יד מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה

translation_notes: The prophecy anticipates killing priests and burning human bones upon an altar. This is corpse desecration and religious violence, not a model for reform.
Jeroboam's temporary hand impairment is not proof that disabled bodies signify sin. Restoration of movement does not establish his moral innocence either.
The man of Divine states a clear boundary and direct command. The old prophet overrides it by claiming equal prophetic status and an angelic message, while the narrator explicitly says he lied.
This is a foundational spiritual-abuse warning: claims such as 'Divine told me' or 'an angel said' do not erase another person's boundaries, prior discernment, consent, or need for verification.
The deceived man is then condemned and killed. Readers should not turn this disturbing sacred-violence narrative into victim-blaming or obedience terror.
The lion and donkey form an extraordinary literary sign. Animal behavior is not a safe modern divination method, and animals are not props for proving religious authority.
The old prophet's mourning and burial care do not erase his deception or responsibility for drawing the man back.
Verse 33 means priests were made from all the people, not necessarily from a socially 'lowest' class; classist translation should be avoided.
Critique of high places must not authorize persecution, vandalism, or contempt toward contemporary religious minorities.
safety_note: Do not use this chapter to justify killing deceived people, disability stigma, corpse desecration, animal omens, or unquestioning obedience to charismatic revelation claims. Verify claimed messages, protect boundaries, hold deceivers accountable, and preserve grief without blaming the manipulated person.
